title: Bengal finds 57,000 'fake' rural housing beneficiaries; 11,000 told to repay by 30 November
dek: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari ordered a criminal investigation as the state released Rs 4,201 crore in second-instalment housing aid to more than 7 lakh families.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Friday that verification of the state's rural housing scheme had identified 57,000 fake beneficiaries, and ordered a criminal investigation. Speaking at a programme at Nabanna, the state secretariat, he said: "Fifty-seven thousand fake beneficiaries have been identified during verification. Legal action will be taken against them."

At the same event the state released Rs 4,201 crore as the second instalment of housing aid to more than 7.17 lakh beneficiaries, according to reports.

## Ineligible recipients told to pay back

Separately from the fake entries, the government said about 12,000 people had received housing money even though they were not eligible. About 1,000 of them have returned it so far, according to reports. The remaining roughly 11,000 have until 30 November to repay, after which they face legal action.

A special investigation team is to be set up to examine the 57,000 cases; one report said it would be led by the state CID. The government has not published the list, the districts involved or the total amount paid out to the fake accounts. Reports differ on the details of the probe, and the state has not issued a written order that The Declaration could read.

## Background

Most of the money now under scrutiny was paid out under the previous Trinamool Congress government. Rural housing in Bengal became a political flashpoint after the Centre stopped releasing funds for the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin in the state in 2022, citing irregularities in beneficiary lists. The then state government launched its own scheme to cover families left out, and the Trinamool accused the Centre of withholding money owed to Bengal's poor.

Since the BJP formed the government in the state this year, Mr Adhikari has made verification of welfare lists a priority. The Trinamool Congress had not responded to Friday's announcement by Saturday morning. Its leaders have previously accused the new government of using investigations to target the party.

According to reports, the Chief Minister also announced cheaper sand for house construction and a Rs 30,000 grant under the housing scheme; the government has not yet published the terms.

## Police modernisation

At a separate event on Friday, the state signed a memorandum of understanding with the Centre on police modernisation and launched a "Police-Mitra" mobile app for citizens. "Police officers need to be provided with modern equipment," Mr Adhikari said. Details of the funding under the agreement were not released.

## What happens next

The 30 November repayment deadline is the first test. Once the investigation team is formed, the questions will be who approved the 57,000 entries, whether officials or local intermediaries took a cut, and how much money can be recovered. Any arrests or charges will be reported when they are made public.
